{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Over 2 million patients in Puerto Rico receive care through Medicare, Medicare Advantage or Medicaid.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Sixty percent of Puerto Rico’s population receives their care through Medicare, Medicare Advantage or Medicaid.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Puerto Ricans pay the same Social Security and Medicare taxes as the fifty states.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Puerto Rico’s Medicaid program receives a 70 percent lower reimbursement rate compared to mainland states.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A federal grant temporarily supplements the low Medicaid reimbursement rate in Puerto Rico, but this grant will soon expire.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for restoring federal Medicaid reimbursement parity for Puerto Ricans.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Access to quality health care is a right, not a privilege.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The federal government has not adequately addressed serious environmental legacy problems stemming from U.S. military exercises in Puerto Rico.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"There has been a decades-long pattern of delay and inaction regarding remediating environmental problems left by the U.S. Navy on the island of Vieques and elsewhere in Puerto Rico.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
